accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS RL.3.1 and RI.3.1 (ask and answer questions, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers) and the England National Curriculum 2013 KS2 Years 3-4 reading comprehension (draw inferences and justify them with evidence from the text). Every lab inference was re-read for a single sound answer: sand + a wave = beach, coat and gloves + a snowman = winter, a lamp + an owl hooting = night; the camel facts were checked (camels can go days without drinking; wide padded feet spread on sand; the hump stores fat, not water).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-comprehension slips: answering from the picture or own life instead of the text (predict: guess because the text will not say), confusing question words (after school given for where, The baby given for when, After lunch for where), a guess no clue supports (Lily is seven, orange juice), a guess a clue contradicts (hot dry day with wet grass, Nothing with an empty glass), and quoting a true but non-proving line (Owls hunt at night; camels live in deserts). The camel hump item deliberately tackles the common water-in-the-hump belief.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagclue is built around this topic's two question kinds: tap word chips that answer who, where and when in one sentence (feedback names the job of the tapped words), hunt exactly two clue chips to reach an unstated place or time, join a clue card and an I know card into a guess dragged into a slot, and tap the camel fact line that proves an answer. It differs from flaginfer (feelings and motives from actions, ages 7-10) and gate_lab_distinct passes on 6-token shingles.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule by doing: a wrong right-there tap explains what the words do (after school tells a time, the question wants a place), the clue hunt counts clues found of 2 and then states clue + clue -> answer, the guess step rejects guesses that ignore or contradict a clue with the reason, and the prove step shows why a true line does not prove the answer. The step summaries only confirm what the taps already showed. Show me completes every task on desktop and iPhone 13.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the step then disproves: to answer Who fed the dog? you should guess because the text will not say (the answer is in the words); for Mia in the sand we cannot tell because it does not say (the clues show the beach); a good guess can be anything that might be true (it must fit every clue, and the lab rejects two that do not).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six fresh challenge items not used in the steps (swimsuit and splash, the baby woke at seven, dripping umbrella, owls in the dark, the milk line, Max to the park), answers rotated each time. Each wrong choice maps to its own why() message naming the slip: a clue says the opposite, no clue says that, those words name who, that is a doing word, after lunch tells when not where, true but about hunting not seeing, and not in the text.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid explanation FK grade -0.7 (target 5.0) in short sentences a five-year-old hears read aloud; adult text FK 8.7 (target 10.0). The lab uses the young class (56px buttons), one instruction per screen such as Tap 2 clue words. Clues found: 0 of 2, and short chips like in the sand. and A wave.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph carries one worked example: the Ben and Pip right-there answers, the Mia clue hunt, the puddle clue + what I know guess, and the camel proof line. The adult text gives the standards, the literal vs inference split, five named mistakes and what the lab does. gate_content passes the filler and similarity checks, including against Inferring Characters' Feelings and Motives (166).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (light) and 360x640 Android (dark) for every step: word chips wrap inside the panel without clipping (Ben / fed / his dog Pip / in the garden / after school.), the two-column clue and I know cards fit at 360px, the three guess strips and four camel lines stay inside the canvas, and every chip has a big button twin below the canvas for small screens.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) with no violations in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, and no console errors. The canvas aria-label is updated by say() with each question, clue found and result; every tap and drag has a real labelled button (Answer with the words in the garden, Clue word: A wave, My guess: It rained., Line 2: ...); colours come from the theme palette.
